references.text: These verses describe the rainbow as the sign of God's covenant with Noah and all living creatures, and they elaborate directly on the meaning of the covenant sign mentioned in verse 12.

God establishes His eternal covenant with Abraham and his descendants (v. 7) and gives circumcision as a sign of the covenant (אוֹת בְּרִית, v. 11), a direct parallel to the covenant sign in Genesis 9:12.
The psalmist recalls God's eternal covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—a covenant He remembers 'forever,' reflecting the eternal nature of God's covenant with Noah.
Isaiah refers directly to Noah's covenant and God's promise that His faithfulness will not depart, confirming the eternal covenant from Genesis 9:12.
God confirms His covenant with day and night and the laws of nature, which cannot be broken—parallel to the unbreakable covenant with Noah in Genesis 9:12.
Jesus is referred to as the great shepherd through the blood of the eternal covenant, which can be seen in light of the eternal covenant God established with Noah.
The eternal covenant with all generations in Noah's time presupposes and is mirrored in the specific covenant with Abraham's offspring.
God's eternal promise to all nations (Gen 9) requires a response to keep the covenant through all generations (Gen 17).
The rainbow as a sign of the old covenant with all creatures presupposes and is mirrored by the blood as a sign of the new covenant.
The universal covenant with all living creatures (Gen 9) finds its specific expression in the covenant with Abraham's descendants (Gen 17).
God's eternal covenant with the nations (Gen 9) reaches its fulfillment in a covenant where God's word and Spirit are placed on children's lips (Isa 59).
The eternal covenant with all generations (Gen 9) is specified and maintained through Isaac's line (Gen 17).
The covenant with all living creatures (Gen 9) is the basis for the promise that all families of the earth will be blessed (Acts 3).
The eternal covenant with an outward sign (Gen 9) presupposes and contrasts with the new covenant with laws written in the heart (Heb 10).
The general covenant with all living creatures (Gen 9) finds its specific expression in the covenant with Abraham (Gen 17).
The promise of a multitude of nations and an eternal inheritance in the covenant with all generations (Gen 9) is confirmed in the blessing to Joseph (Gen 48).
The eternal covenant with an outward sign (Gen 9) presupposes and is mirrored in the new covenant with laws written on the heart (Heb 8).
The rainbow as a sign of the covenant with all living creatures (Gen 9) is mirrored in the Sabbath as a sign of the covenant with Israel (Exod 31).
The eternal covenant with all generations (Gen 9) is mirrored in the eternal covenant with David's line (Isa 55).
The rainbow as a sign of God's grace and protection (Gen 9) is contrasted with the sign of God's judgment (Jer 44).
The eternal covenant with all living creatures (Gen 9) is a concrete example of God's established covenant forever (Ps 111).
